notes.decision: Translated 'their end is there.' Lyc. ⲍⲁⲏ = ϩⲁⲏ 'end, last.' The leer indicates a structural break before ⲧⲧⲉ̄ⲧⲉ.

Lexeme uncertain — possibly 'the half/portion' (ⲧϯⲉ) or 'the joining' (from ⲧⲱⲧ). Left as placeholder pending parallels. The genitive construction ⲧⲧⲉ̄ⲧⲉ ⲛⲧⲉ ⲧⲟⲩⲥⲓⲁ ('X of the substance') is grammatically clear.
Parsed as ⲛⲁϣ- ('be able') + ⲧⲉⲟⲩⲟ ('bring forth/utter') + ⲛ̄- + ⲟⲩⲱⲗⲡ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ ('reveal'). The verb-doubling marks an emphatic apophatic — 'no man can utter or reveal them.'
Translated 'before eternity.' ⲍⲁⲡⲣⲁ = ϩⲁ-ⲡⲣⲟ 'before, in the presence of' (literally 'at the door/face of'). The doubled ⲙⲛ̄ⲛⲧ is likely scribal dittography for ⲙⲛ̄ⲧ-.
ⲟ̄ⲁⲙ = ϭⲟⲙ 'power, ability.' Translated 'power of man' (in negation: 'no human power'). Maintains the apophatic emphasis that the eternal realities cannot be grasped or expressed by human capacity.

ⲭⲉⲥⲧ ⲁⲍⲣⲏⲓ̈ ('convey upward') used here adversatively with ⲟⲩⲃⲉ ('against'): the dark agent rises up against the Light — the cosmic provocation that initiates the mingling. The standard upward-conveyance vocabulary is here turned to oppositional motion.
'To the country of the Living Ones' — the Land of Light. Standard Manichaean cosmological designation; parallel to ⲡⲏⲓ̈ ⲛⲛⲉⲧⲁⲛⲍ 'house of the Living Ones' in line 24.
ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ qualitative 'be mingled' (= ⲙⲟⲩϫⲧ̄). The cosmological key statement: from the moment of opposition, light and darkness, life and death are intermingled — the present cosmic condition.

Lexeme physically present but morphologically unclear. ⲡⲛⲁⲟ̄ = 'the great' (= ⲛⲟϭ); the suffix -ⲛⲉⲟ̄ unidentified. Translated tentatively 'the great combat' from contextual parallelism with ⲡⲙⲓϣⲉ 'the battle' that follows. May be related to ⲛⲁϭ-ⲛⲉϭ or a Lyc orthographic variant of an attested combat-noun.

ⲭⲁⲗⲭ taken as Lyc form of ϫⲱⲗϫ̄/ϫⲱⲗⲕ̄ 'mingle, twist together,' parallel to ⲙⲟⲩⲭⲧ in line 25 and ⲍⲙ ⲡⲙⲟⲩ pattern in line 30. The agent (ⲡⲉⲧⲁⲩ-) is plural — possibly the apostles or the powers — performing the cosmic mingling.

ⲧⲉϩ- = Lyc possessive 'his' (= ⲡⲉϩ- m. / ⲧⲉϩ- f.). 'His substance' and 'his enthumesis' (= ἐνθύμησις, technical Manichaean term for the cosmic 'thought/idea'). The enthumesis here is being introduced as cosmic agent — the matter-thought that organizes itself in the land of darkness.
Read as ⲛ̄-ϩⲏⲧ-ⲥ 'in her,' the Lyc. preposition + 3sg.f. suffix. The bracketed ⲧ is the editor's restoration of the missing letter.

Tentatively understood as a substantivization of Greek παλαμᾶσθαι 'to contrive, work craftily' — 'the contriver' — fitting the cosmogonic context of dark powers. Could alternatively be a proper name. Confidence low.
Read as ϩⲁ-ⲡⲧⲱⲧ 'under/in the agreement,' from ⲧⲱⲧ 'be joined, agreed' (cf. accumulated vocab ⲡⲓⲧⲱⲧ 'the agreement'). The dark powers act in concert.

notes.coptic_form: ⲡⲕⲁⲡⲛⲟⲥ ⲡⲣⲱⲭⲍ ⲡⲧⲧⲏⲩ ⲡⲧⲙⲁⲩ ⲙⲛ̄ ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ
notes.decision: The Five Worlds/Elements of Darkness in canonical order: smoke, fire, wind, water, darkness. The list confirms the chapter is about Matter's emanative cosmogony from the dark abyss.

Reflexive auto-fashioning: 'she molded herself alone.' Matter as both ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲧⲏⲥ ('molder') and ⲡⲗⲁⲥⲙⲁ ('thing-molded') of herself — the self-generation typical of the dark principle in Manichaean cosmogony.
'Many, not in the likeness of one another.' The negation ⲉⲛ marks the heterogeneity of dark emanations, in pointed contrast to the unified likeness of light emanations.
'The storehouses of her Deep' — the dark counterpart to the five Light Storehouses. ⲡⲧⲉⲥⲛⲟⲩⲛ uses the Lyc. 3sg.f. possessive ⲧⲉⲥ-, locating the Deep as Matter's own.
Three verbs of unstable motion: she stood up (ⲧⲱⲕ ⲁⲣⲉⲧ⸗), fell (ⲍⲉⲓ = ϩⲉ), gave way (ⲣ̄-χωρεῖν). The chaotic motion of Matter contrasts with the steady standing-firm of light beings.
'Foul/abominable forms.' ⲉⲧⲃⲁⲓ̈ⲧ tentatively read as qualitative from ⲃⲱⲧⲉ 'abomination, polluted thing.' Confidence moderate.
Tentatively read as ⲁ-ⲩ-ϫⲡⲓⲟ or related verbal form expressing 'they ventured/were eager to make war.' The construction ⲁⲣ̄ ⲟⲩⲡⲟⲗⲉⲙⲟⲥ 'to make a war' is clear; the auxiliary verb is uncertain.
'The lofty kingship' — already in vocabulary, here designating the Light kingdom against which the archons plot war.

Verb of uncertain root, parsed as ⲁ-ϩ- (Lyc. 3pl perfect) + ⲩⲃⲧ + ϩ (Lyc. 3sg.f. object suffix = Sah. -ⲥ). Repeated ⲟⲩⲃⲏⲥ 'against her' across lines 5-6 establishes Hyle/Matter as object. Left untranslated; flagged.
Read as privative ⲁⲧ- + 3sg.f. suffix = 'without her,' though could be a verbal form. Modifies the preceding emanation-from-her clause: the elements emanate 'forth without her' into the smoke.
Four of the five Manichaean dark elements: fire (ⲧⲥⲉ = Sah. ⲥⲁⲧⲉ), wind (ⲡⲧⲏⲩ), water (ⲡⲙⲁⲩ), and Darkness (ⲡⲕⲉⲕⲉ). The fifth — ⲡⲕⲁⲡⲛⲟⲥ 'smoke' — was named in line 13. Standard 5-element inventory.
ⲭⲡⲁⲥ = Lyc. ϫⲡⲟ 'beget, bring forth' with 3sg.f. subject (ⲁⲥ-) and reflexive ⲟⲩⲁⲉⲉⲥ in line 19. The repeated formula ⲙⲡⲥⲏⲩ... ⲉⲧⲁⲥⲭⲡⲁⲥ ⲁⲃⲁⲗ marks two parallel acts of Hyle's bringing-forth.

notes.coptic_form: ⲁⲩⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ ⲛⲧϩⲉ ⲛϩⲃⲥⲱ ⲛ̄ⲩⲏⲣⲉ ⲙⲡⲩⲁⲣⲡ ⲛ̄ⲣⲱⲙⲉ
notes.decision: ⲧⲱϩⲙⲉ from accumulated vocab = 'summon, call forth.' The fruits of Hyle 'are called forth in the manner of garments of the sons of the First Man' — the dark side imitates/mirrors the light cosmogony, where the First Man dons his Five Sons as armor (cf. tamion-passage, K.34).
ⲁⲭⲙ = Lyc. ⲉϫⲙ̄ 'upon.' The fruits/offspring fall upon the earth — the standard motif of the abortive archonic births in Manichaean cosmogony.
'the archon, the wellspring of all demons' — ⲡⲁⲛⲭⲱⲭ here is the dark Hyle/King of Darkness as source of all demonic emanations. Cf. accumulated entry: ⲡⲁⲛⲭⲱⲭ 'wellspring/source' tentative.

ⲫⲛⲁϩ likely = ⲁϥ-ⲡⲱⲍ/ⲡⲱϩ 'he reached' or ⲁϥ-ⲡⲏϩ 'he sprang/went' with directional ⲁϩⲟⲩⲛ 'into.' Translated 'went in unto.' The First Man dons his god-garments — i.e., the Five Light Sons as armor before the cosmic combat.
ⲡⲣ̄ⲓⲱⲩ = plural of ⲡⲣⲏ/ⲡⲣⲓⲉ 'sun, light' — 'the Lights' (cf. ⲡⲡⲣⲓ̈ⲉ 'the Radiance' in glossary). Here likely the divine Light-Emanations with whom the First Man speaks before descent.
Lyc. directional 'upon us' (= Sah. ⲁϫⲱⲛ); fits with κίνδυνοι 'dangers upon us' as standard hardship-formula.
'There being no measure to her' — this stock formula introduces the 'innumerability' theme that runs through the cosmic enumeration of lines 18-23 (sea, firmaments, winds, rivers, dispersed limbs).
